summary: Yohei Kawajiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. Kawajiri held posts at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013 and 2022) and the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Kei Kataoka and Hisataka Ishida. He was a researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).
Yoichi Kawada is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He served as director of the Institute of Oriental Philosophy, attested in 2002 and 2016.
Yong Hua specializes in Buddhist studies. Hua earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries under Sangye Tenzin and Gangru Tsultrim Gyaltsen, later serving at Menri, Triten Norbutse, SOAS (1961), and Munich (1969).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy figure. He studied at Sherab Ling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and served as abbot at Sherab Ling (~1994).
Yongshan He works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at McMaster University under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn (attested 2011) and teachers Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Tsinghua and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Irving Babbitt, later holding posts at Southeast University, Peking University, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Yongyu Chen works in Buddhist studies. Educated with a BA from Cornell and as a PhD student at Harvard, Chen served as a professor at Joong-Ang Sangha University (attested 2015) and an ArtTable Fellow at Public Art Fund (2025).

Yonten Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, completed a diplôme at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and served there as a research advisor in Tibetan Studies.

Yoshifumi Honjo is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Kobe Women's University, Bukkyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Bunkyo University.

Yoshifumi Mizuno specializes in Indology and linguistics. After graduating from Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Toyo Bunko, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto, later becoming a professor there in 2001 and conducting research at the University of Virginia in 1985.
Yoshihiko Amino was a historian and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950). He held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1967–1980) and Kanagawa University (~1980–1995).
Yoshihiko Nasu works in Buddhist studies. Nasu served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and held leadership roles at Kongojushinkai and Kongozyu (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2001). Sakurai has served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and as a researcher at Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center.
Yoshihiro Hayashi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 2009, Hayashi was attested as a part-time lecturer at both Ritsumeikan University and Shitennoji University.
Yoshihiro Matsunami is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a professorship at Taisho University (attested 1991–1999) and served as its president in 2001.

Yoshihito Muroji is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. Muroji has held posts at Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Shiga University of Medical Science.
Yoshiki Motoaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Motoaki held a post at Otani University (attested 2013) and has been affiliated with the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
